segments.text: Goldfish have a three-second memory. Well, that's not exactly true. They can remember things for months.
Scientists have trained goldfish to push levers for food, swim through mazes, and even come over when they hear a certain sound.
Here's the wild part. In one study, goldfish learned to push a lever at the same hour every day, because that was the only hour it worked.
That's not all. Goldfish see more colors than you do, including ultraviolet light.
In fact, with good care a goldfish can live over {20|twenty} years. The oldest one on record made it to {43.|forty-three.}
So next time you forget something, don't call it a goldfish memory. The goldfish might be insulted.
